name: Mariastein
kurzbeschreibung: Tiny village in Tirol with the impressive Mariastein pilgrimage church and castle – a landmark of the Unterinntal valley.
beschreibung:
Overview

Mariastein is an iconic pilgrimage municipality in the Tyrolean Unterinntal within the Kufstein district, situated at an altitude of 575 metres on the sunny, elevated plateau of the Angerberg. Home to approximately 550 residents, Mariastein is one of the smallest communities in Tyrol by population, yet stands as one of the most prominent Marian pilgrimage sites in Austria. The unmistakable local icon is the commanding castle fortress and pilgrimage church of Mariastein, whose massive 42-metre-high tower perches dramatically atop an isolated limestone outcrop overlooking the Inn Valley. Surrounded by pristine meadows, Mariastein brings together profound spiritual peace, royal heritage, and sweeping alpine vistas.

History

The origins of Mariastein date back to the 14th century, when the noble Lords of Freundsberg constructed a fortified residential tower around 1360 to safeguard the ancient road network and river crossing. The transformation into a sacred pilgrimage haven occurred in the 15th century following a widely chronicled miracle associated with a carved Gothic Madonna statue. Consequently, the tower was converted into a vertical castle sanctuary: a wooden stairway of 150 steps leads directly up to the Chapel of Grace on the upper level. Supported by Tyrolean princes, the sanctuary reached its zenith in the 17th century. The castle museum preserves the priceless Tyrolean Archducal Hat of 1602 and the princely scepter—invaluable historical regalia of Tyrol.

Getting There

Mariastein enjoys superb transportation connectivity within the Lower Inn Valley. Motorists depart the A12 Inntal Autobahn at the Wörgl-Ost or Kirchbichl exits and follow the clearly signposted mountain road ascending via Angerberg to Mariastein. Rail passengers take express or regional trains to Wörgl Hauptbahnhof or Kirchbichl along the Unterinntal railway line. From the station forecourts, frequent local buses operated by the Tyrol Public Transport Network run directly up to the pilgrimage church. Cyclists can also ascend via quiet, paved secondary routes branching from the Inn River Cycle Path.

Tips

Climbing the 150 steps inside the castle keep to visit the venerated Chapel of Grace and the Castle Museum, housing the authentic Tyrolean Archducal Hat, provides a memorable encounter with alpine heritage. From the battlements, visitors enjoy sweeping views over the Inn Valley toward the Kaiser Mountains. A nearby natural wonder is hiking to the Buchacker Ice Cave (Hundsalm Eishöhle), the only publicly accessible natural ice cavern in North Tyrol. During summer, the rolling woodland paths across the Angerberg plateau offer refreshing walks and scenic cycling circuits.
